relevance_note: Case report of a Chinese neonate diagnosed with HA20 after array CGH found a heterozygous 5.15 Mb 6q deletion ("The deletion affected at least 30 genes, including TNFAIP3."), plus Table 1 summarising 11 previously published 6q-deletion HA20 patients column by column.
method_note: Read the whole paper; Patient 1 (the first-hand neonate, 'Current report' column) was extracted by hand from the Clinical report text plus her Table 1 column. Table 1 has patients as columns: a header row of sources ('Current report', 'Endo et al.', ...) and a row of labels 'Patient 1'-'Patient 12'; all 12 are in scope (deletions of 6q including TNFAIP3), so each gets a row with the paper's label. A Python script in my scratch directory built the column spans (row label through that patient's cell) and transcribed the cells; I checked every transcribed cell against the table by eye. Table cells contain non-breaking spaces, kept as printed. The table notes define only AIHA and HLH; '+' and '-' are not defined. '+' was read as present; '-' is treated as not reported (v3 rule), so it yields no rows and no exclusions. 'Not mentioned' = not reported. Source columns correspond to reference-list entries: Franco-Jarava et al. = [13] PMID:29572183; Viel et al. = [14] PMID:29678940; Tsuchida et al. = [15] PMID:31164164; Taniguchi et al. = [16] PMID:33446651; Endo et al. = [17] PMID:34520861; Sun et al = [18] PMID:35897075; Wu et al. = [19] PMID:34032947; Wan et al. = [20] PMID:35486341. Whether the two Endo, two Tsuchida or two Wu patients are related is not stated; no family labels given. Inheritance: Table 1 says 'de novo' for Patients 1, 4, 5, 6 and 11, but no parental testing is described, so inheritance is 'not reported' under rule 8 and the table entry is kept in parental_testing_statement. 'paternal' (Patient 2) and 'maternal' (Patient 7) were recorded as inherited paternal/maternal. For Patients 2-12, variant_original_string is the 'Size of deletion' cell, the only variant description printed (no coordinates or breakpoints); zygosity is not stated for them. Pathogenicity 'pathogenic' comes from the Fig. 2 legend ('pathogenic deletions'), which, per the text, summarises all 12 patients. Checklist mappings: Table 1 'Fever' '+' mapped to 'recurrent fever', with the text 'in seven patients, the initial symptoms were unprovoked and recurrent episodes of fever' as a second span (the seven '+' cells match). Also: AIHA -> cytopenia (autoimmune); Henoch-Schönlein purpura (Patient 9) -> vasculitis; Rosacea (Patient 10) -> skin lesions; Gastroenteritis (Patient 4) -> GI inflammation; 'Respiratory- infections' (Patient 4) and 'Infections' (Patient 11) -> recurrent infections. These mappings are judgment calls. For Patient 1, splenomegaly, hepatosplenomegaly and the anemia were not mapped to lymphoproliferation or autoimmune cytopenia. The negative direct antiglobulin test and 'AIHA ... not in accordance with our patient' exclude only AIHA, a narrower item, so cytopenia (autoimmune) stays not reported. A normal brain MRI does not exclude CNS involvement. Normal ophthalmologic assessment was used to exclude uveitis/ocular inflammation, and 'Measurement of autoantibodies ... were normal' to exclude autoantibodies. Age at last evaluation for Patient 1 ('six months') is my reading: the last described assessment is at six months, after which COVID-19 suspended follow-up. The Patient 1 mother is mentioned only by age (29 years, IVF), not as tested or affected, so she gets no row. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) cytoband: the text says '5.15 Mb deletion in 6q23.3q24.3', but the Fig. 1 legend says 'encompassing the 6q23.2q24.3 region'. The text value is recorded. (2) Splenomegaly: the exam ('enlarged liver and spleen ... 2.5 cm below the left costal margin') and Table 1 '+' conflict with 'Abdominal ultrasonography showed no other abnormalitis except for hepatomegaly'. Both rows are emitted; no checklist item is affected. (3) Fever resolution: 'resolved gradually within 24 days' vs CRP 'returned to normal levels accompanied by extinguished fever within 22 days'. (4) TORCH serology including Cytomegalovirus 'were normal', yet CMV was positive by metagenomic sequencing and serum PCR. This is serology vs PCR, so it was not treated as a feature contradiction; CMV DNA recorded as observed.
